candidates.title: Apache Arrow / Parquet - June 2026 meetup in Paris · Luma
candidates.snippet:
​We’re excited to announce the **first ever Apache Arrow and Parquet meetup in Paris!** This meetup will be hosted **on June 18th** by **Datadog**, in their offices, 21 Rue de Châteaudun 75009 Paris.
​[Arrow](https://arrow.apache.org/?utm_source=luma) and [Parquet](https://parquet.apache.org/?utm_source=luma) are two widely-used, open source, language-agnostic data formats for efficient representation of columnar data. They are often complementary: Arrow for in-memory data, Parquet for disk storage.

​The meetup will start at 6:30 pm and will last until 9:30 pm.
## ​Important
​**Please register if (and only if) you plan to show up**, so that we can maximize occupation given a limited number of seats.
​Please show up at the reception desk (21 Rue de Châteaudun) at the ground floor. An agent will welcome you there and check your identity. **Please have the QR code sent by Luma and/or an ID with you (passport or EU identity card).**
## ​Talks
​Talks will be roughly 15 minutes each, with 5 more minutes for questions and answers. All talks will be in English.
​**📌 Zero-Materialization Merging: Concatenating Parquet Files via REE-Encoded Arrow**
​*By Damien Profeta (**[Datadog](https://www.datadoghq.com/?utm_source=luma)**)*
​Traditional compaction is often too CPU-intensive to solve the “small file problem” at scale. This talk introduces Zero-Materialization Merging, which bypasses the costly decode-and-re-encode cycle by concatenating Parquet files through direct [Run-End Encoded (REE)](https://arrow.apache.org/docs/format/Columnar.html?utm_source=luma#run-end-encoded-layout) Arrow manipulation.

Location
Datadog
21 Rue de Châteaudun, 75009 Paris, France
Please show up at the reception desk (21 Rue de Châteaudun) at the ground floor. An agent will welcome you there.

candidates.title: Reliable AI at Scale: Lessons from Dataiku & Mistral AI, mar. 27 oct. 2026, 18:30 | Meetup
candidates.snippet:
Détails Join us on October 27th at 6:30 pm at our Paris office to explore what it really takes to make AI work in the real world. Maxime Appé and Thierry Gengler from Dataiku will show how to keep autonomous LLM agents under control without sacrificing their flexibility. Then Harizo Rajaona from Mistral AI will take us behind the scenes of serving a text-to-speech model at scale, one audio frame at a time. 6:30 – 7:15 pm | Maxime Appé, Technical Product Manager, and Thierry Gengler, Engineering Manager, Dataiku Taming Rogue LLMs:

7:15 – 8:00 pm | Harizo Rajaona, Software Engineer, Mistral AI Deploying and Running a TTS Model: The Fun Part Text-to-speech (TTS) models have improved dramatically in recent years, driven by the rise of Transformer architectures. Training one might sound like the hard part, but wait until you have to serve it at scale! TTS comes with its own set of challenges: tokenizing audio frames without information loss, combining a decoder with flow-matching transformers, and handling real-time streaming. This talk walks through these challenges and the engineering choices involved in building and serving Voxtral TTS, proving that making GPUs actually talk is hard but a lot of fun! The talks will be followed by open discussion and networking. Come ready to ask questions.

candidates.title: Build, Ship, Shape: Amazon Developer Hackathon
candidates.snippet:
#### Welcome to the Amazon Developer Hackathon
For the first time, Fire TV, Alexa+, Ring, and Bee are all part of one global hackathon. Build for one product or use several to connect the living room, the front door, and the cloud. Get started now with our SDKs, simulators, and sample code.
New to building for Amazon devices and services? We'll help you get from idea to submission with documentation and live office hours. Use our AI tools to prototype and troubleshoot along the way.
Choose a track and show off what you build! 🚀
#####
##### Why join?
- Be part of the first hackathon where Fire TV, Alexa+, Ring, and Bee are all open to outside developers at once
- Your product feedback goes directly to the teams building Fire TV, Alexa+, Ring, and Bee
- Compete for a share of $190K value of cash and AWS credits, plus a 1:1 meeting with the Amazon Developer team for track winners
##### Get Started
- Pick your track: Fire TV, Alexa+, Bee, or Ring
- Set up the developer environment for your track (see [Resources](https://amazonappdev2026.devpost.com/resources))
- Review the track details and requirements to start building
- Submit your working demo, code repo, and product feedback by the deadline
### Requirements
#### What to Build
Pick a primary track and ship a working demo. You can layer a mini challenge onto the same project for extra ways to win, but each project can only win one track prize and one mini challenge prize.
**Build or significantly update working applications using Amazon Developer tools into the following primary tracks:**
- **Fire TV
**Launch a demo-ready app on Fire OS or Vega OS. Use React Native, web technologies, or Android (Kotlin/Java), any framework is fine, as long as it runs on Fire OS or Vega OS.
- Priority categories: AI-enhanced viewing, sports, fitness, family entertainment, multi-modal UX, and computer vision.
- **Alexa+
**Experience how brands in Preview are building and shipping experiences on Alexa+ that our customers love:
- Build a self-hosted MCP server (spec 2025-11-25 or later, Streamable HTTP) or an Agent Skill. MCP is the open standard that powers Alexa+ integrations.
- New to MCP? Build a simulated Alexa+ experience in a web app using your preferred agentic tool.
- **Bee (Wearable AI)
**Build a project that connects to real data recorded and processed through a Bee device or an Apple Watch running Bee software, using Bee's CLI, MCP, or Agent Skills. Your demo needs to show your project actually using that data to do something useful for a person.
- Priority use cases: education, developer experience, and personal productivity.
- **Ring
**Build a new app or extend an existing one using Ring APIs, SDKs, simulators, or devices. A physical Ring device is not required.
- Priority categories: access control, business systems, IoT home automation, accessibility, and caretaking.

candidates.title: Inspiring and igniting passion, a ninth-grade internship like no other
candidates.snippet:
Pascale was bowled over by the Amazon Future Engineer program and the professional way her son was welcomed during his mandatory ninth-grade internship in France. The internship presented the different professions within the IT sector and has helped her son clarify his career plan.
Amazon organized a week-long internship for 25 students in the ninth grade at Jean Jaurès middle school, a priority education establishment in Clichy, France. The students were able to discover the different professions within the IT sector, learn about artificial intelligence, attend an introductory lesson on computer coding, and see demonstrations of Alexa-controlled robots. “*The way our children were welcomed, as well as the human and financial resources provided for them, was amazing. They were taken really seriously,”* says Nykou’s mother.

This intensive internship was designed to introduce the children to the world of business and its different careers. The students attended presentations and workshops specifically designed for them by volunteers from Amazon’s workforce. They learned how to code in Scratch. They controlled robots with Alexa. They learned the basics of artificial intelligence and the drone delivery project, Prime Air. They also worked on the attitude they should adopt in a company and identified their strong points to help develop their personality.
After visiting the Clichy and Défense offices, they then went on a virtual visit to a fulfillment center to understand the journey that packages go on. They were also set a challenge! The students were divided into groups of five and asked to imagine what the greatest Amazon innovation might look like in 2040. In true Amazon style, they were told that the sky was the limit, as long as the needs of the customer were met.

This internship has been a wonderful opportunity for the pupils of Jean Jaurès. The Amazon Future Engineer program is both professional and educational, and our children have gained a lot from it. You only have to look at the amazing handbook given to each child at the beginning of the week’s internship. Some 30 pages long, the handbook is full of useful information and was written to help the children in their personal development,”* adds Nykou’s mother.

candidates.title: Forum Icam Entreprises 2026: A Celebration of Networking and Innovation
candidates.snippet:
Entreprises Grands PartenairesIcam
31 Mar 2026
**The Forum Icam Entreprises 2026, held on Friday 27 March** at the Espace Champerret in Paris, was a resounding success! The Icam students from across our various campuses, along with the many companies in attendance — including our Major Partner companies — contributed greatly to this achievement. This 16th edition, powered by the enthusiasm and energy of everyone involved, confirmed that the Forum Icam Entreprises is **a place to connect, a place of opportunity, and a place where career paths take shape**.

Once again this year, conversations were lively and discoveries plentiful, with some outstanding opportunities on offer for our students: **internships, jobs, apprenticeships and volunteer missions.** Several activities made this edition memorable, including a **sophrology introductory workshop** to help students manage pre-interview stress, a **professional photo booth** for headshots, and a prize draw to win **work experience placements at participating industrial companies**.
The highlight of the day was the **Model Mania competition**, co-organised by AvenAo, Prodways Group and Dassault Systèmes. Students were challenged to model a 3D part in record time from a technical drawing using SOLIDWORKS software. Speed, technical skill and creativity were all on show in this hugely popular activity — the winning student completed the challenge in just 3 minutes!

Several conferences punctuated the day, organised by **the Icam Alumni association**, the **Délégation Catholique pour la Coopération** (DCC) — a longstanding partner that opens doors for Icam engineers to engage in international volunteering — and **Apec**.
Participants gained insight into **trends shaping the engineering sector** and identified the key skills needed to meet future challenges. A dedicated conference focused on **what recruiters are looking for in 2026**, featuring speakers including Cyrille Courtier, an Icam alumnus and HR Director at Moët-Hennessy and Dior.
